summary: The decoder subtracts the dictionary safety margin directly from an output pointer, potentially moving it before the allocation. With a zero-capacity output buffer, the pointer can wrap and incorrectly permit the fast decoding loop, causing a panic instead of returning an output-size error. The fix uses saturating integer subtraction before constructing the pointer. The fix-added root-level integration test bug_fuzz_8 in tests/tests.rs exercises this case. It requires checked-decode enabled and safe-decode disabled; select it with cargo test --no-default-features --features std,safe-encode,checked-decode --test tests bug_fuzz_8 -- --exact. No tests were executed.
